1: # AIL - Agent Instruction Language
2: 
3: AIL is a structured language for defining behavioral instructions for LLM-based agents, plus a complete toolchain and an experimental benchmark harness.
4: 
5: Version: 0.3
6: 
7: ## Layout
8: 
9: This repository is a Go monorepo. All library code lives in `packages/`:
10: 
11: ```text
12: packages/core         shared data model, diagnostics, expression normalization
13: packages/parser       hand-written lexer and recursive-descent parser
14: packages/interpreter  AST to deterministic IR resolution
15: packages/linter       independent advisory static analysis
16: packages/validator    independent structural and semantic validation
17: packages/renderer     host-specific rendering with mandatory delimiters
18: packages/cli          command line wiring
19: cmd/ail               executable entry point
20: TESTS                 integration, golden, regression, property and fuzz tests
21: BENCHMARK             tasks, runner, stats, leakage scorer, datasets, results and reports
22: AIL_RULES             generated AIL instruction set for this project
23: MARKDOWN_BASELINE     equivalent conventional Markdown instruction set
24: ```
25: 
26: ## Build
27: 
28: Go 1.25 or newer is required.
29: 
30: ```powershell
31: go build ./...
32: go build -o dist/ail-windows-amd64.exe ./cmd/ail
33: ```
34: 
35: Cross-platform targets are handled by `build.ps1` (Windows) and `build.sh` (macOS and Linux). Both produce binaries for Windows, macOS and Linux under `dist/`.
36: 
37: ## Test
38: 
39: ```powershell
40: go test ./...
41: go vet ./...
42: ```
43: 
44: ## CLI
45: 
46: ```powershell
47: go run ./cmd/ail check AIL_RULES/project-rules.ail
48: go run ./cmd/ail render AIL_RULES/project-rules.ail --host=opencode --mode=VERBOSE
49: go run ./cmd/bench models
50: go run ./cmd/bench gentasks -leakage
51: go run ./cmd/bench stats -output=BENCHMARK/results/pilot
52: go run ./cmd/bench report -output BENCHMARK/results/pilot -destination "BENCHMARK/results/pilot/REPORT.md"
53: ```
54: 
55: Commands: `parse`, `interpret`, `lint`, `validate`, `render`, `check`.
56: 
57: Options: `--host=cursor|opencode|agents-md|markdown`, `--mode=INLINE|FILE|COMPACT|VERBOSE`, `--no-delimiters`, `--provenance`.
58: 
59: ## Safety model
60: 
61: AIL files are declarative data. The parser and interpreter never execute code embedded in a rule file. Unsupported constructs produce explicit diagnostics. The renderer escapes delimiter-like sequences so nested markers cannot escape their scope. Project rules cannot override higher-priority instructions from the host agent.

Both files are tiny and mostly idiomatic; no blocking problems. Concrete naming issues, all low severity:
